sentences.text: The name Serikornis translates to "Ge Sun's silk bird," referencing a specific type of downy body covering seen in the fossil.
This creature is distinguished by having very large front upper jaw teeth that are about twice as long as the others.
The coracoid bone lacks the diagnostic ornamentation of Anchiornis but is elongated to form a crest.
The specimen is nicknamed "Silky" because its delicate hindlimb filaments resemble the modern Silky breed of domestic chicken.
Serikornis was first described in August 2017.
The skeletal morphology suggests Serikornis had a terrestrial ecology without flying adaptations.
The elongated hindlimb feathers suggest they evolved in ground-dwelling maniraptorans before being co-opted for an arboreal lifestyle or gliding.
Phylogenetic analysis places Serikornis as a basal Paravian outside Eumaniraptora.
Some studies place Serikornis in the family Anchiornithidae, grouping it with Eosinopteryx.
Serikornis fossils were found in the Upper Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation in Liaoning, China.
Serikornis lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically the Oxfordian stage, between 163 and 156 million years ago.
The time range for Serikornis is recorded as 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago.
Some researchers believe Serikornis is a junior synonym of Anchiornis.
In 2019, researchers questioned the validity of Serikornis's distinguishing traits, suggesting they might be misinterpreted or intraspecific variation relative to Anchiornis.
